note: Threshold values below are a design proposal, not a measured verdict. No real four-engine (ollama/llama.cpp/mlx/strata) common-result trial exists yet (see README.md); these numbers are illustrative starting points for review and must be recalibrated against a real trial's common JSON before any adoption decision is published.

useCases.label: Interactive coding assistant
useCases.description: A single developer waits on the response in an editor loop. First-token latency and sustained throughput dominate; quality must stay usable but a large model's extra quality is not worth a stall.

rules.rationale: Past ~1.5-1.7s the editor loop reads as hung rather than thinking.
Below ~20 tokens/s, streamed completions render slower than the developer reads/types.
Below 0.75 on the fixed quality rubric, suggestions need manual correction often enough to cost more time than they save.
16 GiB leaves room for the editor, language server and browser on a typical developer machine.

useCases.label: Batch document summarization
useCases.description: An unattended job summarizes many documents overnight. Nothing is waiting on a single response, so latency and per-request throughput matter far less than output quality and fitting the batch host's memory.

rules.rationale: No interactive wait exists; this only guards against a stalled or hanging request.
Sets a floor so the overnight batch window has a bounded worst case, not a target to optimize.
Unattended output reaches a reader without a human re-check, so the quality floor is the highest of the three use cases.
32 GiB matches a dedicated batch host; nothing else runs alongside the job.

useCases.label: Edge / offline device
useCases.description: The engine runs alongside other software on constrained, often battery-powered hardware with no fallback to a larger machine. A low memory ceiling is the binding constraint; speed and quality only need to clear a usability floor.

rules.rationale: A few seconds to first token stays usable for a device assistant that is not a real-time conversation.
5 tokens/s keeps a short reply arriving within a few seconds on constrained hardware.
Lowest floor of the three use cases: the device task set is narrower and the model is the smallest that fits.
4 GiB leaves headroom on an 8 GiB device shared with the OS and other apps.
